tools.name: analyze_directory
tools.description: Tree-view of a directory with LOC, function/class counts, and test markers. Respects .gitignore. Paginates with an opaque cursor; page size is server-owned (50). Large dirs (1000+ files) auto-compact to summary; pass summary=false for the per-file list. git_ref restricts to files changed since a branch/tag/commit.

cursor.description:
Pagination cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor` field. Pass unchanged to retrieve the next page. Omit on the first call.
Must be a valid opaque token or omitted entirely; passing an empty string is invalid and is treated as omitted.
Mutually exclusive with summary=true; passing both returns INVALID_PARAMS.

git_ref.description: Restrict analysis to files changed relative to this git ref (branch, tag, or commit SHA). Empty string or unset means no filtering.

max_depth.description: Maximum directory traversal depth for overview mode only. Default: 3. Pass 0 for unlimited depth. Use 1-3 for large monorepos to manage output size. Ignored in other modes.

summary.description:
true = compact summary (totals plus directory tree, no per-file function lists); false = full output; unset = auto-summarize when output exceeds 50K chars.
Mutually exclusive with cursor; passing both returns INVALID_PARAMS.

files.description: List of files analyzed in the directory

formatted.description: Formatted text representation of the analysis

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor token for the next page of results (absent when no more results)

is_test.description: Whether this file is a test file.

outputSchema.description: Result of directory analysis containing both formatted output and file data.
outputSchema.title: AnalysisOutput

tools.name: analyze_file
tools.description: Functions, types, classes, and imports from a single source file with signatures and line ranges. Fails if directory path supplied; use analyze_directory for directories and analyze_module for a lightweight function/import index (~75% smaller). Paginates with an opaque cursor; page size is server-owned (50). git_ref not supported. Supported: Astro, C/C++, C#, CSS, Fortran, Go, HTML, Java, JavaScript, JSON, Kotlin, Markdown, Python, Rust, TOML, TSX, TypeScript, YAML.

cursor.description:
Pagination cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor` field. Pass unchanged to retrieve the next page. Omit on the first call.
Must be a valid opaque token or omitted entirely; passing an empty string is invalid and is treated as omitted.
Mutually exclusive with summary=true; passing both returns INVALID_PARAMS.

fields.description:
Limit output to specific sections. Valid values: "functions", "classes", "imports", "references", "calls", "all".
The FILE header (path, line count, section counts) is always emitted regardless.
Omitting this field returns all sections (current behavior).
Ignored when summary=true (summary takes precedence).

summary.description:
true = compact summary (totals plus directory tree, no per-file function lists); false = full output; unset = auto-summarize when output exceeds 50K chars.
Mutually exclusive with cursor; passing both returns INVALID_PARAMS.

AnalyzeFileField.description: Output section selector for `analyze_file` fields projection.

oneOf.description: Include function definitions with signatures, types, and line ranges.
Include class and method definitions with inheritance and fields.
Include all sections (equivalent to omitting fields parameter).

formatted.description: Formatted text representation of the analysis

line_count.description: Total line count of the analyzed file

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor token for the next page of results (absent when no more results)

path.description: File path of the analyzed file

semantic.description: Semantic analysis data including functions, classes, and imports

unsupported.description: True when the file extension is not supported; semantic fields are empty and formatted contains a raw preview

arg_count.description: Number of arguments passed at the call site.

inherits.description: Inherited types (parent classes, interfaces, trait bounds)

parameters.description: Parameter list as string representations (e.g., `["x: i32", "y: String"]`).

module.description: Full module path excluding the imported symbol (e.g., `std::collections` for `use std::collections::HashMap`).

calls.description:
Caller-callee pairs extracted from call expressions.
Omitted from output when empty (projection-gated).

imports.description: Flat list of imports; each entry carries its full module path and imported symbols.

references.description: Symbol references. Omitted from output when empty (projection-gated).

tools.name: analyze_module
tools.description: Lightweight function and import index for a single source file with minimal token cost: file name, line count, language, function names with line numbers, and the import list (~75% smaller than analyze_file). Fails if directory path supplied; use analyze_file for signatures, types, or class details. Pagination and git_ref not supported; responses are always a single complete response with no next_cursor field and no follow-up page call. Supported: Astro, C/C++, C#, CSS, Fortran, Go, HTML, Java, JavaScript, JSON, Kotlin, Markdown, Python, Rust, TOML, TSX, TypeScript, YAML.

unsupported.description: True when the file extension is not supported; semantic fields are empty

line.description: Line number where function is defined

ModuleImportInfo.description: Minimal import info for `analyze_module`: module and items only.

outputSchema.description: Minimal fixed schema for `analyze_module`: lightweight code understanding.
outputSchema.title: ModuleInfo

tools.name: analyze_symbol
tools.description: Call graph for a named symbol across all files in a directory. Prefer over analyze_file when the question is "who calls X" or "what does X call" rather than "what is in this file". Modes: call_graph (default), import_lookup (files importing a module path), def_use (write/read sites). Paginates with an opaque cursor; page size is server-owned (20). Fails if file path supplied or if impl_only=true on a non-Rust directory. git_ref restricts to changed files.

cursor.description:
Pagination cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor` field. Pass unchanged to retrieve the next page. Omit on the first call.
Must be a valid opaque token or omitted entirely; passing an empty string is invalid and is treated as omitted.
Mutually exclusive with summary=true; passing both returns INVALID_PARAMS.

git_ref.description: Restrict analysis to files changed relative to this git ref (branch, tag, or commit SHA). Empty string or unset means no filtering.

impl_only.description: Filter callers to impl Trait for Type blocks only. Rust only; returns INVALID_PARAMS for other languages.

match_mode.description: Symbol matching mode (default: exact). exact: case-sensitive exact match. insensitive: case-insensitive exact match. prefix: case-insensitive prefix match. contains: case-insensitive substring match.

max_depth.description: Maximum traversal depth. For call graph mode this is the graph traversal depth (default 1); level 1 = direct callers and callees, level 2 = one more hop, etc. It also caps directory walking. Unset means graph depth 1 and unlimited directory walk. Warn user on levels above 2. Hard cap of 3.

mode.description: Analysis mode. call_graph (default): build a call graph for the symbol. import_lookup: find all files in the directory that import the module path given in symbol (e.g., std::collections); requires symbol to be non-empty and rejects match_mode/max_depth/impl_only. def_use: extract write/read sites for the symbol; requires symbol to be non-empty.

path.description: Directory path to search for the symbol

summary.description:
true = compact summary (totals plus directory tree, no per-file function lists); false = full output; unset = auto-summarize when output exceeds 50K chars.
Mutually exclusive with cursor; passing both returns INVALID_PARAMS.

symbol.description: Symbol name to build call graph for (function or method). Example: `parse_config` finds all callers and callees of that function.

oneOf.description: Build a call graph for the symbol (default).
Find all files in the directory that import the module path given in symbol.
Extract write/read sites for the symbol.

callees.description: Direct (depth-1) callees. `follow_depth` does not affect this field.

callers.description: Direct (depth-1) production callers. `follow_depth` does not affect this field.

def_use_sites.description: Definition and use sites for the symbol.

formatted.description: Formatted text representation of the call graph analysis

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor token for the next page of results (absent when no more results)

test_callers.description: Direct (depth-1) test callers. `follow_depth` does not affect this field.

CallChainEntry.description: Single entry in a call chain (depth-1 direct caller or callee).

file.description: File path relative to the repository root

line.description: Line number of the definition or call site (1-indexed)

symbol.description: Symbol name of the caller or callee

DefUseKind.description: Kind of definition or use of a symbol.

oneOf.description: Augmented assignment (+=, |=, ++, etc.); both written and read.

DefUseSite.description: A single definition or use site of a symbol within a file.

column.description: Column offset (0-indexed, byte offset from line start).

enclosing_scope.description: Name of the enclosing function or method, or None if at file scope.

file.description: File path (relative to the analysis root).

kind.description: Kind of site: write, read, or write_read.

snippet.description: 3-line code context: lines N-1, N, N+1 from source.

tools.name: edit_overwrite
tools.description: Creates or overwrites a file with UTF-8 content; creates parent directories if needed. Works on any file type. Use edit_replace for targeted single-block edits.

path.description: Path to the file to create or overwrite.

working_dir.description: Optional base directory for path resolution (default: server CWD).

bytes_written.description: Number of bytes written (UTF-8 byte length of content).

path.description: Path of the file that was written.

tools.name: edit_replace
tools.description: Replaces an exact text block; old_text must appear exactly once. Fails if zero or multiple matches (extend old_text to disambiguate). replace_all=true replaces every occurrence in one pass. Pass empty new_text to delete. CRLF in old_text normalized to LF; all other whitespace matched exactly. Batch form: pass edits[] (array of {old_text, new_text, replace_all}) instead of old_text/new_text — mutually exclusive — to apply multiple replacements to one file atomically; all edits validate against one content snapshot, any invalid edit aborts the batch with per-index errors and no write, and a successful batch returns per-edit results plus a post-edit content_hash. On invalid_params, re-read with analyze_file or analyze_module and retry. Use edit_overwrite to replace the whole file.

edits.description: Batch edits applied atomically to one file; mutually exclusive with `old_text`/`new_text`.

expected_content_hash.description:
Blake3 hex hash of the raw file bytes the caller last saw. If provided and the file
has changed since the caller last read it, the edit is rejected with `INVALID_PARAMS`
directing the caller to re-read the file. The hash is computed over the raw file bytes
as read by `read_to_string` (i.e. the exact bytes on disk, before any normalization).
Omit to skip the staleness check (backward compatible).

new_text.description: Replacement text; empty string deletes every matched block. Mutually exclusive with `edits`.

old_text.description:
Exact text block to find and replace; must be non-empty. Mutually exclusive with
`edits`: provide either `old_text`/`new_text` (single edit) or `edits` (batch).

path.description: Path to the file to edit.

replace_all.description:
When `true`, replaces every non-overlapping occurrence of `old_text` in a single pass
(sed `s/old/new/g` semantics). Returns `INVALID_PARAMS` if `old_text` is empty.
When `false` (default), `old_text` must appear exactly once; fails with `ambiguous` if
multiple matches are found. Check `occurrences_replaced` in the output to confirm how
many substitutions were made.

working_dir.description: Optional base directory for path resolution (default: server CWD).

BatchEdit.description: One edit item within an `edits[]` batch for `edit_replace`.

old_text.description: Exact text to find within the file.

replace_all.description: When true, replace every non-overlapping occurrence of `old_text`.

bytes_after.description: File size in bytes after the edit.

bytes_before.description: File size in bytes before the edit.

content_hash.description:
Blake3 hex hash of the file bytes after the edit. Present only when the batch
(`edits[]`) form was used.

edits.description: Per-edit results. Present only when the batch (`edits[]`) form was used.

occurrences_replaced.description:
Number of occurrences replaced. Always 1 when `replace_all` is false (default single-match
path). When `replace_all` is true, reflects the actual substitution count (0 triggers a
`not_found` error before this field is populated, so a successful response always has
`occurrences_replaced >= 1`). When the batch (`edits[]`) form is used, this is the
total number of occurrences replaced across all edits in the batch.

path.description: Path of the file that was edited.

BatchEditResult.description: Per-edit result within a successful batch `edit_replace` response.

index.description: Zero-based index of the edit in the `edits[]` request array.

occurrences_replaced.description: Number of occurrences replaced by this edit.

tools.name: exec_command
tools.description: Execute shell command via sh -c (or $SHELL if set); returns stdout, stderr, and exit code. Output capped (30k chars stdout / 10k stderr / 2000 lines); when capped, full captures are exposed as aptu-overflow:// resource links. Set working_dir to the target directory; use relative paths. Pass stdin to pipe UTF-8 content (max 1 MB); heredoc syntax is rejected. For file writes use edit_overwrite or edit_replace. Prefer machine-readable output flags (e.g. --json) to reduce tokens. A 300 s server-side timeout kills runaway children; send notifications/cancelled to cancel early. Built-in filters may strip, cap, or substitute output of known CLI tools (git, cargo); structuredContent names the applied rule and links the full pre-filter output.

command.description: Shell command to execute via sh -c (or $SHELL if set).

stdin.description: UTF-8 content to pipe into the process stdin (max `STDIN_MAX_BYTES` = 1 MB). When None, stdin is closed (null).

working_dir.description: Working directory for the command. Set this instead of prepending cd to the command string. Validated against path traversal; does not sandbox the process.

exit_code.description: Exit code; null if the process could not be waited on (e.g. drain timeout from a background process holding pipes).

filter_applied.description: Description of the filter applied to stdout (if any).

filter_capped.description: True when a built-in filter rule capped the output (max_lines fired).

filter_effect.description: Human-readable description of the filter effect (cap or substitution).

output_collection_error.description:
Set when the post-exit drain timed out because a background process held the
pipes open. Distinct from `output_truncated` (size cap) -- this indicates a
drain timeout rather than a size overflow.

output_truncated.description:
True if the post-exit drain timed out (backgrounded process kept pipes open).
When true, any available output is still included; use the overflow file path
from the truncation notice Content block to recover the full output.

stderr_path.description: Path to the slot file containing full stderr (if output was persisted).

stdout_path.description: Path to the slot file containing full stdout (if output was persisted).

timed_out.description:
True when the command was killed because it exceeded the server execution
timeout or the request was cancelled.
When true, exit_code is None and no partial output is available.

aptu-coder.instructions:
Recommended workflow:
1. Start with analyze_directory(path=<repo_root>, max_depth=2, summary=true) to identify source package (largest by file count; exclude node_modules, vendor, .git, __pycache__, target, dist, build, .venv).
2. Re-run analyze_directory(path=<source_package>, max_depth=2, summary=true) for module map. Include test directories (tests/, *_test.go, test_*.py, test_*.rs, *.spec.ts, *.spec.js).
3. For key files, prefer analyze_module for function/import index; use analyze_file for signatures and types.
4. Use analyze_symbol to trace call graphs.
Prefer summary=true on 1000+ files. Set max_depth=2; increase if packages too large. Paginate with the opaque cursor; page sizes are server-owned (analyze_directory 50, analyze_file 50, analyze_symbol 20).
JSONL metrics at $HOME/.local/share/aptu-coder/ (or $XDG_DATA_HOME/aptu-coder/). Always cd there before jq glob queries.
